board_events.text: At depth $d$, your distance from the centre is $R-d$.
The shell above you exerts ZERO net gravitational force.
Altitude has the factor 2; depth does not — hence $d=2h$ for equal drops.

segments.text: Descending is the subtle one, and it uses the shell theorem beautifully. Go to a depth d, so your distance from the centre is now R minus d.
Split the Earth at your level. Everything above you forms a shell; everything below is an inner sphere, and only that inner sphere will matter.
So your distance from the centre is R minus d, and only the matter enclosed inside that radius pulls you.
By the shell theorem, the spherical shell of matter above you, of thickness d, exerts zero net force. Only the inner sphere pulls you.
Assuming uniform density, the inner sphere's mass is the full mass scaled by R minus d cubed over R cubed.
The acceleration is big G times that inner mass over R minus d squared. Simplify, and it becomes big G M times R minus d over R cubed.
Tidy it against the surface value, and you get the clean result: g at depth equals g times one minus d over R. At the centre it is zero — weightless, though the mass and inertia remain.
<whisper>Notice the contrast: altitude carries a factor of two, depth does not. That is exactly why, for equal small changes in g, the depth is twice the height.
नीचे उतरना subtle वाला है, और यह shell theorem को ख़ूबसूरती से use करता है। एक depth d पर जाइए, तो centre से आपकी दूरी अब R minus d है।
Earth को अपने level पर बाँटिए। आपके ऊपर की हर चीज़ एक shell बनाती है; नीचे की हर चीज़ एक inner sphere, और सिर्फ़ वही inner sphere मायने रखेगा।
तो centre से आपकी दूरी R minus d है, और सिर्फ़ उस radius के अंदर घिरा matter आपको खींचता है।
Shell theorem से, आपके ऊपर का spherical shell, मोटाई d का, zero net force लगाता है। सिर्फ़ inner sphere आपको खींचता है।
Uniform density मानते हुए, inner sphere का mass, पूरे mass को R minus d cubed over R cubed से scale किया हुआ है।
Acceleration है big G into उस inner mass over R minus d squared। simplify कीजिए, और यह बन जाता है big G M into R minus d over R cubed।
इसे surface value के हिसाब से tidy कीजिए, और साफ़ result मिलता है: g at depth बराबर g into one minus d over R। centre पर यह zero है — weightless, हालाँकि mass और inertia तब भी मौजूद।
<whisper>Contrast ग़ौर कीजिए: altitude में two का factor है, depth में नहीं। इसीलिए, g में बराबर छोटी कमी के लिए, depth height की दोगुनी होती है।

board_events.text: The Earth spins, so effective g drops

board_events.caption: At latitude λ, a body circles the axis with radius R cos λ

  <line x1="200" y1="45" x2="200" y2="305" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>
  <text x="208" y="58" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">axis</text>
  <circle cx="278" cy="110" r="5" fill="#22303c"/>
  <text x="288" y="106" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">object</text>
  <line x1="200" y1="110" x2="270" y2="110" stroke="#2b6ca3" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-dasharray="3 2"/>
  <text x="230" y="102" font-size="11" fill="#2b6ca3">R cosλ</text>
  <line x1="272" y1="110" x2="222" y2="110" stroke="#b3402f" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#c7)"/>
  <text x="200" y="160" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">λ</text>
  <text x="220" y="308" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#2f7d5a">g_λ = g minus ω^2 R cos^2λ: max cut at equator, none at poles</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: A body at latitude $\lambda$ moves in a circle of radius $R\cos\lambda$ about the axis.
Part of the true pull supplies this, leaving less to press the body down.
At the equator ($\lambda=0$): maximum cut, $g_{eq}=g-\omega^2 R$.
At the poles ($\lambda=90^\circ$): $\cos\lambda=0$, so rotation has no effect.
Poles also feel heavier because the polar radius is ~21 km smaller ($g\propto 1/R^2$).

segments.text: The last variation is rotation. The Earth spins, so a body is not truly in equilibrium — part of gravity must go toward keeping it turning.
A body at latitude lambda is actually moving in a circle about the rotation axis, and that circle has radius R cos lambda, as the figure shows.
So the body needs a centripetal acceleration, omega squared R cos lambda, directed toward the axis.
Part of the true gravitational pull must supply this centripetal requirement, leaving less to press the body down onto the ground.
Resolving that requirement along the vertical, the effective gravity becomes g minus omega squared R cos squared lambda.
At the equator, lambda is zero and cos lambda is one, so the reduction is greatest: effective g equals g minus omega squared R.
At the poles, lambda is ninety degrees, cos lambda is zero, and rotation has no effect at all — g is largest there.

<curious>And there is a second reason the poles feel heavier: the Earth is slightly flattened, so the polar radius is about twenty-one kilometres smaller, and since g goes as one over R squared, that boosts g further at the poles.
आख़िरी variation है rotation। Earth घूमती है, तो एक body सचमुच equilibrium में नहीं है — gravity का एक हिस्सा उसे घुमाते रहने में लगना चाहिए।
Latitude lambda पर एक body असल में rotation axis के चारों ओर एक circle में घूम रहा है, और उस circle का radius R cos lambda है, जैसा figure दिखाता है।
तो body को एक centripetal acceleration चाहिए, omega squared R cos lambda, axis की तरफ directed।
असली gravitational pull का एक हिस्सा इस centripetal requirement को देना पड़ता है, जिससे body को ज़मीन पर दबाने के लिए कम बचता है।
उस requirement को vertical के साथ resolve करने पर, effective gravity बन जाता है g minus omega squared R cos squared lambda।
Equator पर, lambda zero और cos lambda one है, तो कमी सबसे ज़्यादा है: effective g बराबर g minus omega squared R।
Poles पर, lambda ninety degrees, cos lambda zero है, और rotation का कोई असर नहीं — g वहाँ सबसे बड़ा है।

<curious>और poles के भारी लगने की एक दूसरी वजह भी है: Earth थोड़ी चपटी है, तो polar radius लगभग इक्कीस kilometres छोटा है, और चूँकि g, one over R squared के हिसाब से चलता है, यह poles पर g को और बढ़ाता है।

sections.title: Worked example: surface g and weight at depth R/2 (CBSE)

board_events.text: A planet's g, and a body's weight at depth R/2

board_events.caption: At depth R/2, effective g halves
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 420 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <circle cx="150" cy="115" r="92" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="2"/>
  <circle cx="150" cy="115" r="46" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <circle cx="150" cy="115" r="3" fill="#22303c"/>
  <rect x="142" y="16" width="16" height="12" fill="#c2820a" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="196" y="26" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">200 N (surface)</text>
  <rect x="142" y="61" width="16" height="12" fill="#b3402f"/>
  <text x="196" y="71" font-size="11" fill="#b3402f">100 N (depth R/2)</text>
  <text x="300" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#2f7d5a">g_d = g(1 minus 1/2) = g/2</text>
  <text x="300" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">weight halves; mass unchanged</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: A body weighs 200 N at the surface; find its weight at depth $R/2$.
Weight is $mg$ and depends on location; the body's mass never does.

segments.text: A two-part board example. A planet has mass four point eight times ten to the twenty-four kilograms and radius four times ten to the six metres. First, find the surface g.
Plug into g equals big G M over R squared: six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven, times the mass, over the radius squared.
The numerator is three point two zero times ten to the fourteen; divide by one point six times ten to the thirteen, and g is twenty metres per second squared.
Part two. A body weighs two hundred newtons at the surface. What is its weight at a depth equal to half the radius?
We are given the surface weight, two hundred newtons, and the depth is R over two. Use the depth formula.
g at depth is g times one minus d over R, which is g times one minus one half — exactly g over two.
So the new weight is m times g over two, which is m g over two, two hundred over two, one hundred newtons.
<curious>The body's mass did not change — only the effective g halves at depth R over two, so only the weight halves. Weight is m g and depends on where you are; mass is the same everywhere.
एक दो-हिस्सों वाला board example। एक planet का mass four point eight into ten to the twenty-four kilograms और radius four into ten to the six metres है। पहले surface g निकालिए।
g बराबर big G M over R squared में रखिए: six point six seven into ten to the minus eleven, into mass, over radius squared।
Numerator है three point two zero into ten to the fourteen; one point six into ten to the thirteen से divide कीजिए, और g है twenty metres per second squared।
हिस्सा दो। एक body surface पर दो सौ newtons का weight रखती है। radius के आधे के बराबर depth पर इसका weight क्या है?
हमें surface weight दिया है, दो सौ newtons, और depth R over two है। depth formula use कीजिए।
g at depth है g into one minus d over R, यानी g into one minus one half — बिलकुल g over two।
तो नया weight है m into g over two, यानी m g over two, दो सौ over two, एक सौ newtons।
<curious>Body का mass नहीं बदला — सिर्फ़ effective g depth R over two पर आधा होता है, तो सिर्फ़ weight आधा होता है। weight m g है और इस पर depend करता है कि आप कहाँ हैं; mass हर जगह same है।

sections.title: Worked example: the height where g becomes a quarter (NEET)

board_events.text: At what height does g fall to g/4?

board_events.caption: g/4 means r = 2R, so h = R — not a small height
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 440 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <defs><marker id="c9" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6.5" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="#22303c"/></marker></defs>
  <circle cx="110" cy="120" r="70" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="110" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#22303c">R</text>
  <circle cx="320" cy="120" r="6" fill="#b3402f"/>
  <line x1="110" y1="120" x2="320" y2="120" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <text x="245" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">r = 2R</text>
  <text x="320" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#b3402f">h = R</text>
  <text x="245" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#2f7d5a">g_h = g R^2/(2R)^2 = g/4  (use the exact form)</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Need $g_h=\dfrac{g}{4}$. Use the exact inverse-square form, not the approximation.
Trap: the approximation gives $h=3R/8$ — valid only for $h\ll R$.
When the change in g is large, always use the full $(R+h)^2$ form.

segments.text: A classic NEET speed trap. At what height above the Earth's surface does g become one quarter of its surface value?
The figure flags the danger. A quarter of g means the distance from the centre has doubled, so h equals R — a huge height, not a small one.
So we must use the exact inverse-square form, never the small-height approximation.
Set g times R squared over R plus h squared equal to g over four. The g cancels, leaving R squared over R plus h squared equals one quarter.
Take the square root: R over R plus h equals one half, so R plus h equals two R.
Therefore h equals R. The satellite sits one whole Earth-radius up.

Here is the trap. A hurried student writes g times one minus two h over R equals g over four, and gets h equals three R over eight — completely wrong, because the linear form is valid only for h much smaller than R.
<whisper>Whenever the required change in g is large — a quarter, a ninth — use the full R plus h squared form. Asking is h small before choosing a formula is the entire skill.
एक classic NEET speed trap। Earth के surface से कितनी height पर g अपनी surface value का one quarter बन जाता है?
Figure ख़तरे का संकेत देता है। g का one quarter मतलब centre से distance दोगुनी हो गई, तो h बराबर R — एक बड़ी height, छोटी नहीं।
तो हमें exact inverse-square form use करना होगा, कभी small-height approximation नहीं।
g into R squared over R plus h squared को g over four के बराबर रखिए। g cancel, बचता है R squared over R plus h squared बराबर one quarter।
Square root लीजिए: R over R plus h बराबर one half, तो R plus h बराबर two R।
इसलिए h बराबर R। satellite पूरे एक Earth-radius ऊपर बैठता है।

यहाँ trap है। एक जल्दबाज़ student लिखता है g into one minus two h over R बराबर g over four, और पाता है h बराबर three R over eight — बिलकुल ग़लत, क्योंकि linear form सिर्फ़ h के R से बहुत छोटे होने पर valid है।
<whisper>जब भी g में ज़रूरी बदलाव बड़ा हो — one quarter, one ninth — पूरा R plus h squared form use कीजिए। formula चुनने से पहले is h small पूछना ही पूरी skill है।

board_events.text: How fast must the Earth spin for weightlessness at the equator?

board_events.text: At the equator, $g_{eq}=g-\omega^2 R$. Set it to zero.
That is about 84.6 minutes — a day of roughly 84 minutes.
The Earth spins about 17× slower, so the real equatorial cut in g is tiny.

segments.text: A rotation numerical with a famous answer. How fast would the Earth need to spin for objects at the equator to become weightless, and what day-length is that?
At the equator, the effective gravity is g minus omega squared R. Weightlessness means that effective value drops all the way to zero, as the figure shows.
So set g minus omega squared R equal to zero and solve for the spin rate omega.
Rearranging, omega equals the square root of g over R.
Put in nine point eight for g and six point four times ten to the six for R: omega comes out to one point two four times ten to the minus three radians per second.
The day length is two pi over omega, which is two pi root R over g, about five thousand and seventy-eight seconds.
That is roughly eighty-four point six minutes — a day of about eighty-four minutes instead of twenty-four hours.

<whisper>The Earth actually rotates about seventeen times slower, so the real equatorial reduction in g is only about three hundredths of a metre per second squared. Keep this eighty-four-minute number — it returns in the next example.
एक rotation numerical, एक मशहूर जवाब के साथ। equator पर objects को weightless बनाने के लिए Earth को कितनी तेज़ घूमना होगा, और वो कितनी लंबाई का दिन है?
Equator पर, effective gravity है g minus omega squared R। weightlessness का मतलब वो effective value पूरी तरह zero तक गिर जाए, जैसा figure दिखाता है।
तो g minus omega squared R को zero के बराबर रखकर spin rate omega के लिए हल कीजिए।
Rearrange करने पर, omega बराबर square root of g over R।
g के लिए nine point eight और R के लिए six point four into ten to the six रखिए: omega निकलता है one point two four into ten to the minus three radians per second।
Day length है two pi over omega, यानी two pi root R over g, लगभग पाँच हज़ार अठहत्तर seconds।
यह लगभग eighty-four point six minutes है — twenty-four hours के बजाय लगभग चौरासी मिनट का दिन।

<whisper>Earth असल में लगभग सत्रह गुना धीमी घूमती है, तो g में असली equatorial कमी सिर्फ़ लगभग तीन सौवें हिस्से metre per second squared की है। यह चौरासी-मिनट का number याद रखिए — यह अगले example में लौटता है।

sections.title: Worked example: a tunnel through the Earth is SHM (JEE Advanced)

board_events.text: Drop a ball down a tunnel through the Earth's centre

board_events.caption: The net pull is a restoring force toward the centre
board_events.svg:

  <line x1="188" y1="45" x2="188" y2="285" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <line x1="212" y1="45" x2="212" y2="285" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>

  <text x="240" y="132" font-size="11" fill="#b3402f">F = minus (mg/R) r</text>
  <text x="200" y="308" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" fill="#2f7d5a">SHM: T = 2π√(R/g) about 84 min</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Inside, at distance $r$, only the sphere of radius $r$ pulls: $g(r)=g\,r/R$.
The minus sign: the force always points back toward the centre.
This is Hooke's law $F=-k_{\text{eff}}\,r$, with $k_{\text{eff}}=mg/R$.

segments.text: A cross-chapter gem. Drill a frictionless tunnel straight through the centre of the Earth, drop a ball in from the surface, and show it performs simple harmonic motion.
Look at the ball a distance r from the centre. By the shell theorem, only the sphere of radius r pulls it; the outer shell contributes nothing.
From the depth result, the local gravitational acceleration at radius r is g times r over R, directed toward the centre.
So the force on a ball of mass m is minus m g over R, times r.
That minus sign is the whole point: the force always points back toward the centre, the equilibrium point, opposing the displacement.
This is exactly Hooke's law, force equals minus k effective times r, with an effective spring constant m g over R. Any such force gives simple harmonic motion.
The angular frequency is the square root of k effective over m, which is the square root of g over R.

<excited>So the period is two pi root R over g, about eighty-four point six minutes — the same magic number as the weightless-equator day and a surface-skimming satellite. Three different problems, one period. That deep unification is what JEE Advanced rewards.
एक cross-chapter रत्न। Earth के centre के सीधे आर-पार एक frictionless tunnel खोदिए, surface से एक ball गिराइए, और दिखाइए कि यह simple harmonic motion करती है।
Centre से distance r पर ball को देखिए। shell theorem से, सिर्फ़ radius r का sphere इसे खींचता है; बाहरी shell कुछ contribute नहीं करता।
Depth result से, radius r पर local gravitational acceleration है g into r over R, centre की तरफ directed।
तो mass m की ball पर force है minus m g over R, into r।
वो minus sign ही असली बात है: force हमेशा centre की तरफ, equilibrium point की तरफ वापस point करता है, displacement का विरोध करते हुए।
यह बिलकुल Hooke's law है, force बराबर minus k effective into r, एक effective spring constant m g over R के साथ। ऐसा कोई भी force simple harmonic motion देता है।
Angular frequency है square root of k effective over m, यानी square root of g over R।

<excited>तो period है two pi root R over g, लगभग eighty-four point six minutes — वही magic number जो weightless-equator day और surface-skim करते satellite का है। तीन अलग problems, एक period। यही गहरा unification JEE Advanced reward करता है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for g

board_events.text: g: the traps and the shortcuts
1. Altitude approx only for small h — else use $g R^2/(R+h)^2$.
2. 'Height has the 2, depth does not': $(1-2h/R)$ vs $(1-d/R)$, so $d=2h$.
3. g depends on the planet, not the falling body — heavy and light fall alike.
4. Equator is lighter from BOTH the bulge and the spin — name both.
Reason in ratios: $g\propto M/R^2$, or $g\propto\rho R$ at fixed density.
Same density? $g\propto R$. Same mass? $g\propto 1/R^2$.
Memorise the magic period $T=2\pi\sqrt{R/g}\approx 84$ min.

segments.text: Let us close Part three with the g traps and the ratio shortcuts that save time.
Trap one: using the altitude approximation when h is not small. It holds only for small heights. For satellites or any h comparable to R, use the exact g R squared over R plus h squared.

Trap two: swapping the altitude and depth formulae. Altitude carries a factor of two, depth does not. Memorise: height has the two, depth does not — which is why, for equal small changes, the depth is twice the height.
Trap three: thinking g depends on the falling body. It does not — g is fixed by the planet's mass, radius, density, and rotation. Weight depends on the body; g does not.
Trap four: crediting only rotation, or only shape, for the lighter equator. Both act together — the bulge and the rotational reduction. Name only one in a board answer and you lose marks.
Now the shortcuts. For any compare-two-planets problem, reason in ratios: g goes as M over R squared, or equivalently as rho times R.
Pick the form that isolates what you are comparing. If density is fixed, g tracks R. If mass is fixed, g fights R squared.
<whisper>And memorise the magic period: two pi root R over g, about eighty-four minutes — the tunnel oscillation, a surface satellite, and the weightless equatorial day, all in one number.
Part three को g के traps और time बचाने वाले ratio shortcuts के साथ ख़त्म करते हैं।
Trap one: altitude approximation तब use करना जब h छोटा न हो। यह सिर्फ़ छोटी heights के लिए है। satellites या R के comparable किसी भी h के लिए, exact g R squared over R plus h squared use कीजिए।

Trap two: altitude और depth formulae आपस में बदल देना। altitude में two का factor है, depth में नहीं। याद रखिए: height में two है, depth में नहीं — इसीलिए बराबर छोटे बदलाव के लिए depth height की दोगुनी है।
Trap three: यह सोचना कि g गिरते body पर depend करता है। नहीं करता — g planet के mass, radius, density, और rotation से तय होता है। weight body पर depend करता है; g नहीं।
Trap four: हल्के equator के लिए सिर्फ़ rotation, या सिर्फ़ shape को श्रेय देना। दोनों साथ काम करते हैं — bulge और rotational कमी। board answer में सिर्फ़ एक बताया तो marks गए।
अब shortcuts। किसी भी compare-two-planets problem के लिए, ratios में reason कीजिए: g, M over R squared के हिसाब से चलता है, या बराबर रूप से rho into R।
वो form चुनिए जो आपकी comparison वाली quantity को अलग करे। density fixed हो तो g, R को track करता है। mass fixed हो तो g, R squared से लड़ता है।
<whisper>और magic period याद रखिए: two pi root R over g, लगभग चौरासी मिनट — tunnel oscillation, एक surface satellite, और weightless equatorial day, सब एक number में।

sections.title: Gravitational energy, and why it is negative

board_events.text: Energy stored in where masses sit
Lift a stone: you store energy in the stone–Earth system; let go and it returns as motion.

board_events.caption: U vs r: a valley that lies entirely below zero
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 460 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <line x1="55" y1="58" x2="435" y2="58" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <line x1="55" y1="48" x2="55" y2="255" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="40" y="54" font-size="12" fill="#22303c">U</text>
  <text x="440" y="62" font-size="12" fill="#22303c">r</text>
  <text x="60" y="52" font-size="10" fill="#22303c">0</text>
  <path d="M78,250 C120,150 175,100 255,84 C345,70 405,64 432,62" fill="none" stroke="#2f7d5a" stroke-width="2.6"/>
  <text x="300" y="120" font-size="13" fill="#2f7d5a">U = -GMm/r</text>
  <text x="235" y="272" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#b3402f">always negative; reaches 0 only at infinity; deeper = more tightly bound</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Set the zero of energy at infinity, where the masses barely feel each other.
Bring a mass inward: gravity does POSITIVE work, like a ball rolling into a valley.
The system gives up energy, so its stored energy drops below zero.
The deeper you go (smaller $r$), the more negative $U$ becomes.
The negative sign is the signature of an attractive, bound system.

segments.text: So far we tracked the gravitational force. This subtopic is about gravitational energy — the energy stored simply in how masses are arranged.
Lift a stone and you have stored energy in the stone-and-Earth system. Let go, and that stored energy turns straight back into motion.
Here is the idea that trips up almost everyone, so let us meet it head on: gravitational potential energy is negative. The graph shows why — a valley lying entirely below zero.
First we choose our zero. When the two masses are infinitely far apart they barely feel each other, so we call the stored energy zero there — a clean starting line.
Now bring a mass in from infinity toward the Earth. Gravity is attractive, so it pulls the mass inward and does positive work, like a ball rolling down into a valley, speeding up on its own.
Since the system gives up energy — it could have done work for you — its stored energy drops below the zero line.
And the deeper you go, the smaller r, the more negative the potential energy becomes.
<curious>So that negative sign is not a mistake. It is the very signature of an attractive force and a bound system.
अब तक हमने gravitational force track किया। यह subtopic gravitational energy के बारे में है — वो energy जो सिर्फ़ इसमें store होती है कि masses कैसे arrange हैं।
एक पत्थर उठाइए और आपने stone-and-Earth system में energy store कर दी। छोड़िए, और वो stored energy सीधे वापस motion में बदल जाती है।
यहाँ वो idea है जो लगभग सबको उलझाता है, तो इसे सीधे सामना करते हैं: gravitational potential energy negative होती है। graph दिखाता है क्यों — एक valley जो पूरी तरह zero के नीचे है।
पहले zero चुनते हैं। जब दोनों masses infinitely दूर हों, वे मुश्किल से एक-दूसरे को महसूस करते हैं, तो हम वहाँ stored energy को zero कहते हैं — एक साफ़ starting line।
अब एक mass को infinity से Earth की तरफ अंदर लाइए। gravity attractive है, तो यह mass को अंदर खींचती है और positive work करती है, जैसे एक ball valley में लुढ़कती हुई, ख़ुद ही तेज़ होती।
चूँकि system energy छोड़ता है — यह आपके लिए काम कर सकता था — इसकी stored energy zero line के नीचे गिर जाती है।
और जितना गहरा जाइए, r जितना छोटा, potential energy उतनी ही ज़्यादा negative होती जाती है।
<curious>तो वो negative sign कोई ग़लती नहीं है। यह एक attractive force और एक bound system की असली पहचान है।

sections.title: The valley in action: binding, escape, and black holes

board_events.text: One picture explains the whole subtopic
A more negative $U$ means the masses are more tightly bound.
A satellite's total energy is negative: it is trapped in the valley.
Escaping needs a minimum launch speed: enough energy to climb to the rim.

board_events.caption: Shrink the body and the escape speed climbs
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 470 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <defs><marker id="d2" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="7" refY="4.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,4.5 L0,9 Z" fill="#2f7d5a"/></marker></defs>
  <circle cx="80" cy="130" r="46" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.6"/>
  <line x1="80" y1="80" x2="80" y2="40" stroke="#2f7d5a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#d2)"/>
  <circle cx="230" cy="130" r="30" fill="#e6ebee" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.6"/>
  <line x1="230" y1="96" x2="230" y2="30" stroke="#2f7d5a" stroke-width="2.4" marker-end="url(#d2)"/>
  <circle cx="380" cy="130" r="16" fill="#22303c"/>
  <line x1="380" y1="110" x2="380" y2="24" stroke="#b3402f" stroke-width="2.8" marker-end="url(#d2)"/>
  <text x="380" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#b3402f">v_e = c</text>
  <text x="235" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" fill="#22303c">shrink R and the escape speed climbs: v_e = √(2GM/R)</text>
  <text x="235" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#b3402f">push it far enough and nothing escapes — a black hole</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Keep $M$ but shrink $R$: the well steepens and $v_e=\sqrt{2GM/R}$ grows.
Push until $v_e$ equals the speed of light — nothing escapes: a black hole.
A black hole is just gravity's valley made infinitely steep.

segments.text: This single valley picture explains nearly everything in the subtopic, so let us cash it out.
First, a more negative potential energy means the two masses are more tightly bound. You would have to supply energy to pull them apart.
Second, a satellite's total energy is negative — it is trapped in the valley, which is exactly what keeps it in a closed orbit.
Third, escaping requires a minimum launch speed: just enough energy to climb all the way up to the rim, out to infinity.
Now push the picture. Keep the same mass but squeeze it into a smaller and smaller radius. The well at the surface gets steeper.
As R shrinks, the escape speed, root two G M over R, climbs higher and higher.
Push it to the extreme, to a radius where the escape speed would equal the speed of light itself. At that point nothing, not even light, can climb out.
<excited>That object has become a black hole — simply gravity's valley made infinitely steep, the same physics of bound, negative-energy systems taken to its limit.
यही एक valley तस्वीर subtopic की लगभग हर चीज़ समझाती है, तो इसे भुनाते हैं।
पहला, ज़्यादा negative potential energy का मतलब दोनों masses ज़्यादा tightly bound हैं। उन्हें अलग करने के लिए आपको energy देनी होगी।
दूसरा, एक satellite की total energy negative है — यह valley में फँसा है, और यही इसे एक closed orbit में रखता है।
तीसरा, escape करने के लिए एक minimum launch speed चाहिए: बस इतनी energy कि rim तक, infinity तक चढ़ सके।
अब तस्वीर को आगे धकेलिए। वही mass रखिए पर उसे छोटे-से-छोटे radius में निचोड़िए। surface पर well steeper होता जाता है।
जैसे R घटता है, escape speed, root two G M over R, ऊँची से ऊँची होती जाती है।
इसे extreme तक धकेलिए, एक ऐसे radius तक जहाँ escape speed ख़ुद light की speed के बराबर हो जाए। उस point पर कुछ भी, यहाँ तक कि light भी, बाहर नहीं निकल सकता।
<excited>वो object एक black hole बन गया — बस gravity की valley को infinitely steep बना दिया गया, वही bound, negative-energy systems की physics अपनी हद तक ले जाई गई।

sections.title: Two clarifications: system energy, and potential per kilogram

board_events.text: Whose energy is it, and what is potential?

board_events.caption: U belongs to the pair; V is energy per kilogram
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 460 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <circle cx="120" cy="95" r="26" fill="#c2820a" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1.4"/>
  <text x="120" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#22303c">M</text>
  <circle cx="300" cy="95" r="16" fill="#2b6ca3"/>
  <text x="300" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#ffffff">m</text>
  <line x1="146" y1="95" x2="284" y2="95" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <path d="M120,135 L120,150 L300,150 L300,135" fill="none" stroke="#b3402f" stroke-width="1.4"/>
  <text x="210" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#b3402f">U belongs to the pair, not to one body</text>
  <text x="230" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#2f7d5a">V = U/m: potential is energy per kilogram, a property of the place</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Potential energy belongs to the SYSTEM, not to one body.
'The stone's PE' is only loose shorthand.
Treat $U$ as a property of the whole arrangement.
Gravitational potential $V$ is that same energy measured per kilogram.
$V$ is a property of the location itself, independent of what you place there.
Relation: $U=mV$ — the per-kilogram value times the mass you place.

segments.text: Two clarifications keep students out of trouble for the rest of the subtopic.
The first is about ownership. Potential energy belongs to the system of two masses together, not to either one alone.
It makes no real sense to say the stone has a certain potential energy. The energy lives in the configuration of stone and Earth together.
When we casually say the stone's potential energy, we are only using shorthand. Keep the system in mind, especially in multi-body problems.
So treat U as a property of the whole arrangement, and be careful when a problem seems to hand it to one object.
The second clarification introduces potential. Gravitational potential, capital V, is that same stored energy but measured per kilogram.
That makes V a property of the location itself, out there in space, independent of whatever test mass you later place at that point.
<curious>And the link between them is simple: U equals m times V. Find the per-kilogram potential, then multiply by the mass you actually put there.
दो clarifications आपको बाक़ी subtopic में मुसीबत से बचाती हैं।
पहली ownership के बारे में है। potential energy दो masses के system की है, किसी एक अकेले की नहीं।
यह कहने का असल में कोई मतलब नहीं कि पत्थर के पास एक ख़ास potential energy है। energy stone और Earth के साथ वाले configuration में रहती है।
जब हम casually कहते हैं पत्थर की potential energy, तो बस shorthand use कर रहे होते हैं। system याद रखिए, ख़ासकर multi-body problems में।
तो U को पूरे arrangement की property मानिए, और सावधान रहिए जब कोई problem इसे एक object को थमाती दिखे।
दूसरी clarification potential लाती है। gravitational potential, capital V, वही stored energy है पर per kilogram नापी गई।
यह V को ख़ुद location की property बनाता है, space में वहाँ, चाहे आप बाद में उस point पर कोई भी test mass रखें।
<curious>और इनके बीच का link सीधा है: U बराबर m into V। per-kilogram potential निकालिए, फिर उस mass से multiply कीजिए जो आप सचमुच वहाँ रखते हैं।

sections.title: Potential energy of two masses, by integration

board_events.text: Deriving $U=-GMm/r$

board_events.caption: Bring m from infinity to r; gravity does positive work
board_events.svg:

  <text x="80" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#22303c">M</text>
  <line x1="108" y1="100" x2="300" y2="100" stroke="#22303c" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
  <text x="200" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">r</text>
  <circle cx="300" cy="100" r="8" fill="#2b6ca3"/>
  <text x="410" y="104" font-size="11" fill="#22303c">from infinity</text>
  <line x1="392" y1="100" x2="330" y2="100" stroke="#2f7d5a" stroke-width="2.2" marker-end="url(#d4)"/>
  <text x="240" y="138" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#2f7d5a">gravity does positive work bringing it in</text>
  <text x="235" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#b3402f">U(r) = -W_grav = -GMm/r</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: By definition, $U(r)$ is minus the work gravity does bringing $m$ in from infinity.
Negative because gravity did positive work, so the system released energy.
For $n$ particles, sum over all $\tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$ pairs. Surface: $U=-\dfrac{GMm}{R}$.

segments.text: Let us derive the potential energy of two particles — the result CBSE asks for.
Fix a mass M and bring a test mass m in from infinity to a distance r. As the figure shows, gravity pulls it inward and does positive work along the way.
By definition, the potential energy at r is minus the work done by gravity in this process.
So U of r equals minus the integral, from infinity to r, of the gravitational force dotted with the displacement.
The force has magnitude big G M m over x squared and points inward. Doing the integral from infinity to r gives plus big G M m over r.
Therefore U of r equals minus that work, which is minus big G M m over r.
It comes out negative because gravity did positive work, so the system released energy, dropping below the infinity reference of zero.
For a system of many particles, just sum this over all distinct pairs: minus big G, sum over pairs, of m i m j over r i j.
<whisper>There are n times n minus one over two pairs in all. And at the Earth's surface, a mass m has potential energy minus big G M m over R.
आइए दो particles की potential energy derive करें — वही result जो CBSE पूछता है।
एक mass M fix कीजिए और एक test mass m को infinity से distance r तक अंदर लाइए। जैसा figure दिखाता है, gravity इसे अंदर खींचती है और रास्ते भर positive work करती है।
Definition से, r पर potential energy, इस process में gravity के किए work का negative है।
तो U of r बराबर minus वो integral, infinity से r तक, gravitational force dot displacement का।
Force का magnitude है big G M m over x squared और यह अंदर point करता है। infinity से r तक integral करने पर मिलता है plus big G M m over r।
इसलिए U of r बराबर minus वो work, यानी minus big G M m over r।
यह negative निकलता है क्योंकि gravity ने positive work किया, तो system ने energy छोड़ी, infinity के zero reference के नीचे गिरते हुए।
कई particles के system के लिए, बस इसे सभी distinct pairs पर sum कीजिए: minus big G, sum over pairs, m i m j over r i j।
<whisper>कुल मिलाकर n into n minus one over two pairs होते हैं। और Earth के surface पर, एक mass m की potential energy है minus big G M m over R।

sections.title: Gravitational potential: per-kilogram energy that adds as a scalar

board_events.text: Potential $V=U/m=-GM/r$

board_events.caption: Potential adds as a scalar — just sum the numbers

board_events.text: $V$ is the work per kilogram to bring a test mass from infinity to that point.
Potential is a scalar: add algebraically, with signs — no components.
The field is the negative slope of potential: downhill, high to low.
Surface: $V=-\dfrac{GM}{R}=-gR$. Dimensions $[V]=[L^2T^{-2}]$.

segments.text: Now potential, the per-kilogram cousin of potential energy, and the reason it makes many problems fast.
Divide the energy by the test mass and you get V equals U over m, which is minus big G M over r. Turn it around, and U equals m times V.
Here is why potential is so friendly. It is a scalar, so from several masses you just add the numbers, each with its sign — no components, no angles.
In words, V is the work done per kilogram to carry a small test mass from infinity to that point — a property of the field at that location.
For many masses, V is minus big G times the sum of m i over r i. A quick algebraic sum, far easier than the corresponding force problem.
Say it clearly: potential is a scalar. Add it algebraically with signs, never as vectors.
And the bridge to the field: the field is the negative derivative of the potential, E g equals minus d V by d r.
So the field always points downhill on the potential landscape, from high potential to low.
<whisper>Two anchors for the exam: at the surface V is minus big G M over R, which is minus g R; and the dimensions of V are L squared T to the minus two.
अब potential, potential energy का per-kilogram भाई, और वो वजह जिससे यह कई problems तेज़ बना देता है।
Energy को test mass से divide कीजिए और मिलता है V बराबर U over m, यानी minus big G M over r। उलटिए, और U बराबर m into V।
यहाँ potential इतना friendly क्यों है। यह एक scalar है, तो कई masses से आप बस numbers जोड़ते हैं, हर एक अपने sign के साथ — कोई components नहीं, कोई angles नहीं।
शब्दों में, V वो work per kilogram है जो एक छोटे test mass को infinity से उस point तक लाने में लगता है — उस location पर field की property।
कई masses के लिए, V है minus big G into sum of m i over r i। एक तेज़ algebraic sum, संबंधित force problem से कहीं आसान।
साफ़ कह दीजिए: potential एक scalar है। इसे signs के साथ algebraically जोड़िए, कभी vectors की तरह नहीं।
और field का पुल: field, potential का negative derivative है, E g बराबर minus d V by d r।
तो field हमेशा potential landscape पर downhill point करता है, high potential से low की तरफ।
<whisper>Exam के लिए दो anchors: surface पर V है minus big G M over R, यानी minus g R; और V के dimensions हैं L squared T to the minus two।

sections.title: Escape velocity, from energy conservation

board_events.text: The minimum speed to reach infinity

board_events.caption: Reach infinity with zero KE: KE at surface + PE = 0

board_events.text: To escape means to reach infinity ($U=0$) with at least zero kinetic energy.
The body's mass cancels — escape velocity is independent of the escaping mass.
Also independent of launch direction, since energy is a scalar.
For the Earth, $v_e\approx 11.2$ km/s.
And $v_e=\sqrt{2}\,v_o$ — root-two times the surface orbital speed.

segments.text: Escape velocity is the minimum speed to break free of a planet forever, and energy conservation delivers it in a few lines.
To escape means to just reach infinity, where the potential energy is zero, arriving with at least zero kinetic energy — no energy to spare.
Gravity is conservative, so total mechanical energy is conserved. Set the total energy at the surface equal to the minimum total energy at infinity, which is zero plus zero.
That is one half m v e squared, the kinetic energy at the surface, plus minus big G M m over R, the potential energy there, all equal to zero.
Solve, and the escape velocity is root two big G M over R. Using big G M equals g R squared, this is also root two g R.
Notice the body's mass cancels out of the energy equation. Escape velocity is independent of the escaping body's mass — a pebble and a spaceship need the same speed.
It is independent of launch direction too, because energy is a scalar and does not care which way you point.
For the Earth, plugging in the numbers gives about eleven point two kilometres per second.
<whisper>A link worth memorising: escape velocity is root two times the orbital velocity of a surface-skimming satellite. Know one, and you instantly know the other.
Escape velocity एक planet से हमेशा के लिए मुक्त होने की minimum speed है, और energy conservation इसे कुछ lines में दे देता है।
Escape करने का मतलब बस infinity तक पहुँचना, जहाँ potential energy zero है, कम से कम zero kinetic energy के साथ आते हुए — कोई energy बचाकर नहीं।
Gravity conservative है, तो total mechanical energy conserve होती है। surface पर total energy को infinity पर minimum total energy के बराबर रखिए, जो zero plus zero है।
यानी one half m v e squared, surface पर kinetic energy, plus minus big G M m over R, वहाँ potential energy, सब zero के बराबर।
हल कीजिए, और escape velocity है root two big G M over R। big G M बराबर g R squared use करने पर, यह root two g R भी है।
ग़ौर कीजिए body का mass energy equation से cancel हो जाता है। escape velocity escape करते body के mass से independent है — एक कंकड़ और एक spaceship को same speed चाहिए।
यह launch direction से भी independent है, क्योंकि energy एक scalar है और इसे परवाह नहीं कि आप किधर point करते हैं।
Earth के लिए, numbers रखने पर लगभग eleven point two kilometres per second मिलता है।
<whisper>याद रखने लायक़ एक link: escape velocity, surface skim करते satellite की orbital velocity की root two गुना है। एक जानिए, और दूसरी तुरंत पता।

board_events.text: Inside a thin shell: $V=-\dfrac{GM}{R}$ (constant, equal to the surface value).
Outside either body: $V=-\dfrac{GM}{r}$, just like a point mass.
Deepest potential at the centre, yet zero field there — flat, not zero.
Self-energy: the energy released assembling the body from dust at infinity.

segments.text: For JEE, the potential inside extended bodies and one more quantity, the self-energy, round out the subtopic.
Look at the potential of a solid sphere versus r. Outside it behaves like a point mass; inside it dips to its deepest value at the very centre.
Start with a thin shell. Inside it, the potential is not zero — it is a constant, minus big G M over R, equal to the surface value.
Both a shell and a solid sphere, from the surface outward, give minus big G M over r, exactly like a point mass.
Inside a solid sphere the potential is minus big G M over two R cubed, times the quantity three R squared minus r squared.
At the surface this reduces to minus big G M over R, as it must; and at the centre it reaches its most negative value, minus three big G M over two R, one and a half times the surface value.
So the potential is deepest at the centre, even though the field there is zero — a vivid reminder that zero field means flat potential, not zero potential.
Finally, the gravitational self-energy of a uniform sphere is minus three big G M squared over five R.
<excited>That is the energy released in assembling the whole body from dust scattered at infinity — the very energy that powers gas clouds collapsing into stars.
JEE के लिए, extended bodies के अंदर potential और एक और quantity, self-energy, subtopic को पूरा करती हैं।
एक solid sphere का potential r के मुक़ाबले देखिए। बाहर यह एक point mass की तरह behave करता है; अंदर यह ठीक centre पर अपनी सबसे गहरी value तक dips करता है।
एक thin shell से शुरू कीजिए। इसके अंदर potential zero नहीं है — यह एक constant है, minus big G M over R, surface value के बराबर।
एक shell और एक solid sphere दोनों, surface से बाहर, minus big G M over r देते हैं, बिलकुल एक point mass की तरह।
एक solid sphere के अंदर potential है minus big G M over two R cubed, into तीन R squared minus r squared।
Surface पर यह minus big G M over R बन जाता है, जैसा होना चाहिए; और centre पर यह अपनी सबसे negative value तक पहुँचता है, minus three big G M over two R, surface value का डेढ़ गुना।
तो potential centre पर सबसे गहरा है, हालाँकि वहाँ field zero है — एक साफ़ याददिहानी कि zero field का मतलब flat potential है, zero potential नहीं।
आख़िर में, एक uniform sphere की gravitational self-energy है minus three big G M squared over five R।
<excited>यह वो energy है जो पूरे body को infinity पर बिखरी धूल से जोड़ने में release होती है — वही energy जो gas clouds को stars में ढहने की ताक़त देती है।

board_events.text: Masses 2, 4, 6 kg on a side-3.0 m triangle. Find the system's PE.
Three particles give three pairs, all at the same 3.0 m here.
Negative: energy must be supplied to disperse the masses to infinity.

segments.text: A clean board example on system potential energy. Three point masses — two, four, and six kilograms — sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle of side three metres. Find the total potential energy.
The figure is the key. A three-particle system has three distinct pairs, and here every pair is separated by the same three metres.
So we add the potential energy of each pair. With a common separation r, factor it out and sum the products of the masses.
That is minus big G over r, times the quantity m one m two plus m one m three plus m two m three.
Put in the numbers: minus six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven, over three, times eight plus twelve plus twenty-four.
The bracket is forty-four, so the energy is minus six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven over three, times forty-four — minus nine point seven eight times ten to the minus ten joules.
Notice how the common separation made this painless: one factor of minus big G over r, and just the sum of the three mass-products inside.
<curious>The value is negative, which means you would have to supply energy to pull the three masses apart and scatter them back to infinity.
System potential energy पर एक साफ़ board example। तीन point masses — दो, चार, और छह kilograms — side तीन metres के equilateral triangle के कोनों पर हैं। total potential energy निकालिए।
Figure ही key है। एक three-particle system में तीन distinct pairs होती हैं, और यहाँ हर pair उसी तीन metres से अलग है।
तो हम हर pair की potential energy जोड़ते हैं। एक common separation r के साथ, इसे बाहर निकालिए और masses के products को sum कीजिए।
यानी minus big G over r, into m one m two plus m one m three plus m two m three।
Numbers रखिए: minus six point six seven into ten to the minus eleven, over three, into eight plus twelve plus twenty-four।
Bracket है forty-four, तो energy है minus six point six seven into ten to the minus eleven over three, into forty-four — minus nine point seven eight into ten to the minus ten joules।
ग़ौर कीजिए common separation ने इसे कितना आसान बना दिया: minus big G over r का एक factor, और अंदर बस तीन mass-products का sum।
<curious>Value negative है, जिसका मतलब तीनों masses को अलग करके वापस infinity तक बिखेरने के लिए आपको energy देनी होगी।

board_events.text: Earth's $v_e$ is 11.2 km/s. Planet: mass $2M_E$, radius $R_E/2$.
Trap: applying the factor without the root gives 44.8 km/s — wrong.
Escape velocity scales as $\sqrt{M/R}$: apply inside the root, take it once.

segments.text: A quick NEET ratio problem. The Earth's escape velocity is eleven point two kilometres per second. Find the escape velocity from a planet with twice the Earth's mass and half its radius.
Reason in ratios, do not recompute. Since escape velocity is root two big G M over R, it is proportional to the square root of M over R.
Compare the planet with the Earth: its mass is doubled and its radius is halved, and we track both together inside the root.
So the ratio of escape velocities is the square root of the mass ratio over the radius ratio — the square root of two over one half.
Two over one half is four, and the square root of four is two. So the planet's escape velocity is twice the Earth's.
That gives two times eleven point two, which is twenty-two point four kilometres per second.
The trap is to forget the square root and report the factor of four, giving forty-four point eight, or to confuse escape velocity with orbital velocity.
<whisper>Remember the shape: escape velocity scales as the square root of M over R. Apply the factors inside the root, then take the root once.
एक तेज़ NEET ratio problem। Earth की escape velocity eleven point two kilometres per second है। Earth के दोगुने mass और आधे radius वाले planet से escape velocity निकालिए।
Ratios में reason कीजिए, दोबारा compute मत कीजिए। चूँकि escape velocity root two big G M over R है, यह M over R के square root के proportional है।
Planet की Earth से तुलना कीजिए: इसका mass double और radius आधा है, और हम दोनों को root के अंदर साथ track करते हैं।
तो escape velocities का ratio है mass ratio over radius ratio का square root — two over one half का square root।
Two over one half है four, और four का square root है two। तो planet की escape velocity Earth की दोगुनी है।
इससे मिलता है two into eleven point two, यानी twenty-two point four kilometres per second।
Trap है square root भूलकर four का factor बताना, जिससे forty-four point eight मिलता है, या escape velocity को orbital velocity से confuse करना।
<whisper>Shape याद रखिए: escape velocity, M over R के square root के हिसाब से चलती है। factors root के अंदर लगाइए, फिर एक बार root लीजिए।

board_events.text: Lift slowly to height $R$, so KE is unchanged: $W=\Delta U$.
The school shortcut gives $mgh=mgR$ — exactly double the true answer.
Use $mgh$ only when $h\ll R$.

segments.text: A JEE Main example that exposes the limits of the m g h shortcut. Lift a body slowly from the Earth's surface to a height equal to the Earth's radius R. Find the work done against gravity.
Because we lift slowly, kinetic energy does not change, so the work done against gravity equals the change in potential energy, as the figure sets up.
The final separation is R plus h. With h equal to R, that is two R from the centre.
So the work is the final potential energy minus the initial: minus big G M m over R plus h, minus minus big G M m over R, with h equal to R.
Put in R plus R equals two R. The work becomes minus big G M m over two R plus big G M m over R, which is big G M m over two R.
Substitute big G M equals g R squared, and the work simplifies neatly to one half m g R.
Compare with the school shortcut. m g h, with h equal to R, gives m g R — exactly double the true answer. The reason: m g h assumes constant g, but over a height R gravity weakens a lot.
<whisper>So the true work is one half m g R, and m g h overestimates it by a factor of two here. Use m g h only when h is much smaller than R.
एक JEE Main example जो m g h shortcut की हद उजागर करता है। एक body को Earth के surface से Earth के radius R के बराबर height तक धीरे-धीरे उठाइए। gravity के ख़िलाफ़ किया work निकालिए।
चूँकि हम धीरे उठाते हैं, kinetic energy नहीं बदलती, तो gravity के ख़िलाफ़ किया work, potential energy के बदलाव के बराबर है, जैसा figure set करता है।
Final separation है R plus h। h बराबर R के साथ, यह centre से two R है।
तो work है final potential energy minus initial: minus big G M m over R plus h, minus minus big G M m over R, h बराबर R के साथ।
R plus R बराबर two R रखिए। work बनता है minus big G M m over two R plus big G M m over R, यानी big G M m over two R।
big G M बराबर g R squared रखिए, और work साफ़-सुथरे one half m g R में simplify हो जाता है।
School shortcut से तुलना कीजिए। m g h, h बराबर R के साथ, देता है m g R — असली जवाब का बिलकुल दोगुना। वजह: m g h मानता है g constant, पर R जितनी height पर gravity काफ़ी weak हो जाती है।
<whisper>तो असली work है one half m g R, और m g h इसे यहाँ दो के factor से ज़्यादा आँकता है। m g h सिर्फ़ तब use कीजिए जब h, R से बहुत छोटा हो।

board_events.caption: Momentum splits the released energy unequally

board_events.text: Masses $m$ and $2m$, only mutual gravity. Find the relative velocity at separation $r$.
Substitute $v_1=2v_2$: the kinetic sum becomes $3m v_2^2$.
You cannot split the energy in half — momentum decides the share.

segments.text: A JEE Advanced problem where two conservation laws work together. Masses m and two m are released from rest in deep space, separated by a distance d, with only their mutual gravity acting. Find their relative velocity of approach when the separation has shrunk to r.
Two laws are in play. No external force acts, so total momentum is conserved; and gravity is conservative, so total mechanical energy is conserved.
Momentum first. Starting from rest, the total momentum stays zero, so m v one equals two m v two.
That immediately gives v one equals two v two — the lighter mass moves twice as fast.
Now energy conservation. Initial kinetic energy is zero, so minus two big G m squared over d equals the kinetic terms minus two big G m squared over r.
Substitute v one equals two v two into the kinetic energy. The two kinetic terms combine into three m v two squared.
Solve for v two squared: it is two big G m over three, times one over r minus one over d.
The relative velocity of approach is v one plus v two, which is three v two, equal to the square root of six big G m times one over r minus one over d.

<excited>The key lesson: you cannot simply give each mass half the released energy. The lighter mass moves faster and carries more kinetic energy — momentum conservation is what correctly splits the share.

एक JEE Advanced problem जहाँ दो conservation laws साथ काम करते हैं। masses m और two m को deep space में rest से छोड़ा जाता है, distance d से अलग, सिर्फ़ उनकी mutual gravity act करते हुए। जब separation सिमटकर r हो जाए, उनकी relative velocity of approach निकालिए।
दो laws खेल में हैं। कोई external force नहीं, तो total momentum conserve होता है; और gravity conservative है, तो total mechanical energy conserve होती है।
पहले momentum। rest से शुरू, total momentum zero रहता है, तो m v one बराबर two m v two।
यह तुरंत देता है v one बराबर two v two — हल्का mass दोगुनी तेज़ चलता है।
अब energy conservation। initial kinetic energy zero है, तो minus two big G m squared over d बराबर kinetic terms minus two big G m squared over r।
v one बराबर two v two को kinetic energy में substitute कीजिए। दोनों kinetic terms मिलकर three m v two squared बनते हैं।
v two squared के लिए हल कीजिए: यह two big G m over three, into one over r minus one over d है।
Relative velocity of approach है v one plus v two, यानी three v two, बराबर square root of six big G m into one over r minus one over d।
<excited>अहम सबक़: आप हर mass को आधी released energy नहीं दे सकते। हल्का mass तेज़ चलता है और ज़्यादा kinetic energy ले जाता है — momentum conservation ही सही share बाँटता है।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for potential and energy

board_events.text: Energy: the traps and the shortcuts
1. Never drop the negative: $U=-GMm/r$, $V=-GM/r$. Positive would mean repulsion.
2. $mgh$ only for $h\ll R$ — else use $\Delta U=-GMm(1/r_f-1/r_i)$.
3. $V$ is per kilogram (J/kg); $U=mV$ is the total (J). Do not mix them.
4. Zero field ≠ zero potential: inside a shell $E=0$ but $V=-GM/R$.
Potential adds like a scalar; force adds like a vector — compute $V$ first.
Pro-tip: get $U=mV$ or speeds via energy conservation, all from a scalar sum.
Pro-tip: the √2 bridge — $v_e=\sqrt{2}\,v_o$; Earth: $v_o\approx7.9$, $v_e\approx11.2$ km/s.

segments.text: Let us close Part four with the energy traps and the shortcuts that make these problems fast.
Trap one, the most frequent of all: dropping the negative sign. Both U and V are negative; writing them positive reverses the physics — it would imply repulsion. Always carry the minus.

Trap two: using m g h for large heights. That is only the change in potential energy when h is much smaller than R. For heights comparable to R, use the exact change, minus big G M m times one over r final minus one over r initial.

Trap three: confusing potential with potential energy. V is per unit mass, in joules per kilogram; U equals m V is the total energy, in joules. Mixing their units, or forgetting the factor of m, loses marks instantly.

Trap four, the deep one again: zero field does not mean zero potential. Inside a shell the field is zero, yet the potential is a non-zero constant, minus big G M over R. Field is the slope of potential, not the potential itself.
Now the shortcuts. Potential adds like a scalar, while force adds like a vector. So for several masses, just add the numbers for V, then get energy or speed from it.
That single habit — compute V first, then U equals m V, or use energy conservation — makes potential problems far faster than the matching force problems.

<whisper>And remember the root-two bridge: escape velocity is root two times the surface orbital speed. For the Earth, orbital is about seven point nine, escape about eleven point two kilometres per second.
Part four को energy के traps और उन shortcuts के साथ ख़त्म करते हैं जो इन problems को तेज़ बनाते हैं।
Trap one, सबसे common: negative sign गिरा देना। U और V दोनों negative हैं; इन्हें positive लिखना physics उलट देता है — यह repulsion बताएगा। हमेशा minus साथ रखिए।

Trap two: बड़ी heights के लिए m g h use करना। यह सिर्फ़ potential energy का बदलाव है जब h, R से बहुत छोटा हो। R के comparable heights के लिए, exact बदलाव use कीजिए, minus big G M m into one over r final minus one over r initial।

Trap three: potential को potential energy से confuse करना। V per unit mass है, joules per kilogram में; U बराबर m V total energy है, joules में। इनके units mix करना, या m का factor भूलना, तुरंत marks गँवाता है।

Trap four, फिर गहरा वाला: zero field का मतलब zero potential नहीं। shell के अंदर field zero है, फिर भी potential एक non-zero constant है, minus big G M over R। field, potential का slope है, potential ख़ुद नहीं।
अब shortcuts। potential एक scalar की तरह जुड़ता है, जबकि force एक vector की तरह। तो कई masses के लिए, बस V के numbers जोड़िए, फिर उससे energy या speed निकालिए।
यही एक आदत — पहले V निकालिए, फिर U बराबर m V, या energy conservation use कीजिए — potential problems को मिलती-जुलती force problems से कहीं तेज़ बना देती है।
<whisper>और root-two bridge याद रखिए: escape velocity, surface orbital speed की root two गुना है। Earth के लिए, orbital लगभग seven point nine, escape लगभग eleven point two kilometres per second।

board_events.text: Fire a cannonball hard enough and it never lands

board_events.caption: Increasing speed: short arc, longer arc, then a closed orbit

board_events.text: Fire gently and it arcs down nearby; fire harder and it lands farther.
Fire hard enough and the Earth curves away as fast as the ball falls.
It keeps falling forever and never lands — that is an orbit.
A satellite is not escaping gravity or balancing it — it is in perpetual free fall.
The Moon, the Space Station, a relay — all endlessly falling around the Earth.
This single image is the key to the whole subtopic.

segments.text: Picture standing on top of an impossibly tall mountain and firing a cannonball horizontally. This is Newton's own thought experiment, and it unlocks the whole subtopic.
Fire it gently, and it arcs down and lands nearby. The figure shows what happens as you fire harder and harder.
Fire it harder and it lands much farther away, the Earth's surface curving a little beneath its path.
Now fire it hard enough, and something magical happens: the ball falls toward the Earth at exactly the rate the round Earth curves away under it.
So it keeps falling forever and never lands. That is an orbit.
A satellite — the Moon, the International Space Station, a communications relay — is not escaping gravity, and it is not balancing gravity. It is in perpetual free fall.
It is endlessly falling around the Earth, held on its curved path by nothing but gravity.
<curious>Hold on to this single image. Everything else in the subtopic is just this picture, made precise.
एक बेहद ऊँचे पहाड़ की चोटी पर खड़े होकर एक cannonball को horizontally फ़ायर करने की कल्पना कीजिए। यह Newton का अपना thought experiment है, और यह पूरे subtopic को खोल देता है।
इसे धीरे फ़ायर कीजिए, यह नीचे curve होकर पास गिरती है। figure दिखाता है कि जैसे-जैसे आप ज़्यादा ज़ोर से फ़ायर करते हैं, क्या होता है।
ज़ोर से फ़ायर कीजिए और यह बहुत दूर गिरती है, Earth की surface उसके रास्ते के नीचे थोड़ा curve होती हुई।
अब इतना ज़ोर से फ़ायर कीजिए, और कुछ जादुई होता है: ball, Earth की तरफ ठीक उसी rate से गिरती है जिस rate से गोल Earth उसके नीचे से मुड़ जाती है।
तो यह हमेशा के लिए गिरती रहती है और कभी नहीं गिरती। यही एक orbit है।
एक satellite — Moon, International Space Station, एक communications relay — gravity से escape नहीं कर रहा, और gravity को balance भी नहीं कर रहा। यह perpetual free fall में है।
यह लगातार Earth के चारों ओर गिरता रहता है, अपने curved path पर सिर्फ़ gravity के सहारे टिका।
<curious>इस एक तस्वीर को पकड़े रहिए। subtopic की बाक़ी हर चीज़ बस यही तस्वीर है, precise बनाई गई।

board_events.text: Three crisp rules the planets obey

board_events.text: First law: orbits are ellipses, with the Sun at one focus — not the centre.
Second law: a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times.
So it races near the Sun and dawdles when far — angular momentum in disguise.
Third law: the period squared grows as the orbit size cubed, $T^2\propto a^3$.
Mercury laps the Sun in 88 days; distant Pluto takes 248 years.
Newton's inverse-square gravity reproduces all three automatically.

segments.text: Long before Newton, Johannes Kepler stared at decades of Tycho Brahe's planetary data and distilled three crisp rules. He did not know why they held — that took Newton — but the rules were exact.
The figure captures the first two. Orbits are ellipses, and the planet sweeps out area at a steady rate.
First law, the law of orbits: every planet moves in an ellipse, with the Sun sitting at one focus — not at the centre.
Second law, the law of areas: the line from the Sun to the planet sweeps equal areas in equal times.
That is why a planet races when near the Sun and dawdles when far. As we will see, this is really the conservation of angular momentum, wearing a geometric costume.
Third law, the law of periods: the square of the orbital period grows as the cube of the orbit's size, T squared proportional to a cubed.
So bigger orbits mean much longer years. Mercury whips around the Sun in eighty-eight days, while distant Pluto takes two hundred forty-eight years.
<excited>And here is the beautiful part: Newton's inverse-square gravity reproduces all three of these laws automatically. We will derive the third in just a few lines.
Newton से बहुत पहले, Johannes Kepler ने दशकों के Tycho Brahe के planetary data को देखा और तीन साफ़ rules निकाले। उन्हें पता नहीं था कि ये क्यों टिके रहते हैं — वो Newton ने बताया — पर rules exact थे।
Figure पहले दो को पकड़ता है। orbits ellipses हैं, और planet एक steady rate से area sweep करता है।
पहला law, law of orbits: हर planet एक ellipse में चलता है, Sun एक focus पर बैठा — centre पर नहीं।
दूसरा law, law of areas: Sun से planet तक की line बराबर समय में बराबर areas sweep करती है।
इसीलिए एक planet Sun के पास तेज़ दौड़ता है और दूर सुस्त हो जाता है। जैसा हम देखेंगे, यह असल में angular momentum का conservation है, एक geometric पोशाक में।
तीसरा law, law of periods: orbital period का square, orbit के size के cube के हिसाब से बढ़ता है, T squared proportional to a cubed।
तो बड़ी orbits मतलब बहुत लंबे साल। Mercury Sun के चारों ओर अठासी दिन में घूम जाता है, जबकि दूर Pluto को दो सौ अड़तालीस साल लगते हैं।
<excited>और ख़ूबसूरत बात: Newton की inverse-square gravity इन तीनों laws को अपने-आप reproduce करती है। हम तीसरे को बस कुछ lines में derive करेंगे।

board_events.text: An astronaut in the Space Station is NOT beyond Earth's pull.
Gravity there is nearly as strong as on the ground — about 90%.
They float because they and the spacecraft are both in free fall together.
It is the same floating you would feel in a lift whose cable snapped.
A satellite's total energy is negative — it is bound in the gravitational valley.
Negative total energy is the signature of a closed, bound orbit.

segments.text: Two ideas confuse students constantly, so let us settle them before the formulas. The first is weightlessness.
Weightlessness is not the absence of gravity. An astronaut floating in the Station is not beyond the Earth's pull at all.
Say it plainly: the astronaut is not beyond Earth's gravity. At that altitude gravity is still doing almost all of its work.
In fact gravity there is roughly ninety percent of its surface value — nearly as strong as on the ground.
They float because they and their spacecraft are both falling together, in free fall, so there is no contact force between astronaut and floor.
It is the very same floating you would feel in a lift whose cable suddenly snapped — everything falling at once, so nothing presses on anything.
The second idea: a satellite's total energy is negative. Being bound in the gravitational valley, its energy lies below the zero we set at infinity.
<curious>And that negative total energy is exactly the mathematical signature of a bound, closed orbit — not a quirk, but the definition of being trapped.
दो ideas students को लगातार उलझाते हैं, तो formulas से पहले इन्हें सुलझाते हैं। पहला है weightlessness।
Weightlessness gravity की ग़ैर-मौजूदगी नहीं है। Station में तैरता astronaut Earth के pull से परे बिलकुल नहीं है।
साफ़ कह दीजिए: astronaut Earth की gravity से परे नहीं है। उस altitude पर gravity अब भी अपना लगभग पूरा काम कर रही है।
असल में वहाँ gravity अपनी surface value का लगभग नब्बे percent है — ज़मीन जितनी ही strong।
वे तैरते हैं क्योंकि वे और उनका spacecraft दोनों साथ गिर रहे हैं, free fall में, तो astronaut और floor के बीच कोई contact force नहीं।
यह वही तैरना है जो आप एक lift में महसूस करेंगे जिसकी cable अचानक टूट जाए — सब कुछ एक साथ गिरता, तो कुछ किसी पर दबाव नहीं डालता।
दूसरा idea: एक satellite की total energy negative है। gravitational valley में bound होने से, इसकी energy उस zero के नीचे है जो हमने infinity पर रखा।
<curious>और वो negative total energy ही एक bound, closed orbit की गणितीय पहचान है — कोई quirk नहीं, बल्कि फँसे होने की परिभाषा।

sections.title: Two useful satellites: geostationary and polar

board_events.text: High-and-fixed, or low-and-sweeping

board_events.caption: Geostationary hovers over the equator; polar scans strips
